questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the long-run Phillips curve is vertical
questions.stem: An amateur astronomer logs that inflation has run above target for two years while unemployment sits at its natural rate; what does the long-run tradeoff imply?

options.text: Unemployment returns to the natural rate regardless of inflation
Higher inflation permanently lowers unemployment below the natural rate
options.misconception: confuses short-run tradeoff with long-run outcome

options.text: Inflation must fall to zero before unemployment stabilizes
options.misconception: assumes price stability is required for equilibrium

options.text: The natural rate rises whenever inflation exceeds target
options.misconception: treats inflation as shifting structural unemployment

questions.explanation: In the long run money is neutral, so unemployment returns to the natural rate at any inflation rate. The tempting idea that sustained inflation can buy permanently lower unemployment fails once expectations adjust.
questions.hint: Think about money neutrality in the long run

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why sticky nominal wages deepen a recession
questions.stem: Log entry: a telescope maker's nominal wages cannot fall even as prices drop; explain how this rigidity affects employment.

answer.exemplar: When nominal wages are rigid downward, a fall in prices raises real wages above market-clearing levels, so firms cut hiring and employment falls, deepening the recession until prices or wages adjust.

questions.stem: Log note: nominal wage rigidity combined with deflation can lead to what macro problem?

options.text: Rising real wages and falling employment

questions.explanation: Deflation with rigid nominal wages raises real wages and cuts employment. The tempting idea that deflation boosts real income ignores the employment cost.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain productivity sources
questions.stem: An astronomer logs rising labor productivity; which factor most directly raises it?
questions.explanation: Productivity rises with technology and capital per worker. The tempting idea that more workers raise productivity confuses total output with output per hour.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain underemployment
questions.stem: Log entry: part-time workers wanting full-time work are not counted as unemployed; this understates what?
questions.explanation: Underemployment means official unemployment understates true labor market slack. The tempting idea that it only affects the natural rate confuses measurement with equilibrium.
